title: Your Financial Playbook for Uncertain Times
description: Navigating economic uncertainties requires a well-structured and adaptable financial plan. Diversifying your investments across various asset classes like equ.

faq.q: How much emergency fund is truly enough?
faq.a: Generally, 3-6 months of essential expenses is recommended. However, for self-employed individuals or those with volatile income, 9-12 months might be more prudent to provide a larger buffer against income disruptions.

faq.q: Should I stop my SIPs during market downturns?
faq.a: It's generally advised to continue SIPs during market downturns. This allows you to buy more units when prices are low, which can lead to higher returns when markets recover, a strategy known as rupee cost averaging.

faq.q: Is gold a good investment for long-term goals?
faq.a: Gold can be a good diversifier and a hedge against inflation and market volatility, but it may not always outperform equities over very long periods. A small allocation (5-15%) to gold can add stability to a portfolio.

faq.q: How often should I review my financial plan?
faq.a: You should ideally review your financial plan at least once a year, or whenever there's a significant life event such as a job change, marriage, birth of a child, or a major economic shift.

faq.q: What are the tax benefits of NPS?
faq.a: NPS offers tax benefits under Section 80C (up to ₹1.5 lakhs), an additional deduction of up to ₹50,000 under Section 80CCD(1B), and employer contributions are deductible under Section 80CCD(2) up to 10% of salary.

faq.q: How can I manage my home loan effectively in uncertain times?
faq.a: Consider making partial prepayments whenever possible to reduce the principal and interest burden. Also, explore options to switch to a lower interest rate if available, though be mindful of any associated charges.

based_on.title: Mint Money Festival: a financial playbook for uncertain times

fact_check.summary: The article provides generally accurate financial advice, but contains a few inaccuracies regarding specific tax sections and the nature of returns for certain instruments.

corrections.note: Corrected the reference to National Savings Certificates and clarified the specific sections of the Income Tax Act under which NPS offers tax benefits, including the employer contribution limit.

edits.why: NPS Trust is the National Pension System Trust, which manages the NPS, not a debt instrument itself. National Savings Certificates (NSC) are the correct government-backed debt option. PPF and NSC offer tax benefits and assured returns.
